rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says he will meet his community entering Paradise without reckoning, in repeated groups, distinguished by the traces of ablution.
rows.anchor: فإذا هم غر محجلون من آثار الوضوء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet urges marriage and increased descendants, saying he will take pride in their number before other communities, even including miscarried infants.
rows.anchor: تناكحوا تناسلوا تكثروا ، فإني أباهي بكم الأمم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's immense community is a great blessing warranting mention as al-Kawthar; boasting even of an infant makes this abundance especially fitting.
rows.anchor: فكيف بمثل هذا الجم الغفير ، فلا جرم حسن منه تعالى أن يذكره

rows.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة
rows.claim: One interpretation is the Prophet's many virtues: he is superior to all prophets, and kawthar describes a generous man rich in good.
rows.anchor: قال المفضل بن سلمة : يقال رجل كوثر إذا كان سخيا كثير الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexicographers also define kawthar as a master possessing abundant good, supporting the interpretation as the Prophet's many virtues.
rows.anchor: الكوثر } السيد الكثير الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the Prophet's elevated mention, already explained through God's promise to raise his renown.
rows.anchor: القول العاشر : الكوثر رفعة الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is knowledge: knowledge is abundant good, and God gave the Prophet knowledge and commanded him to seek more; wisdom is likewise called abundant good.
rows.anchor: القول الحادي عشر : أنه العلم قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues kawthar should be a worldly gift already bestowed, since the wording says “We have given”; knowledge and prophethood are the noblest such gifts.
rows.anchor: نعم الجنة سيعطيها لا أنه أعطاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the command to pray follows the gift, knowledge is a fitting interpretation: recognizing God precedes worship, as in other passages.
rows.anchor: ولأن فاء الموجب للعبادة ليس إلا العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is good character, whose benefit reaches learned and ignorant people, humans and animals, more widely than knowledge does.
rows.anchor: أن الكوثر هو الخلق الحسن ، قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's good character showed itself in his care for strangers and in praying for guidance for people who broke his tooth.
rows.anchor: اللهم اهد قومي فإنهم لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the Praiseworthy Station, meaning intercession; Razi links it to protection in this life and the Prophet's intercession for major sinners.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث عشر : الكوثر هو المقام المحمود الذي هو الشفاعة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet reserved his answered supplication to intercede for his community on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قال عليه السلام : ( إن لكل نبي دعوة مستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies al-Kawthar with this very surah, which is short yet encompasses the benefits of both worlds.
rows.anchor: القول الرابع عشر : أن المراد من الكوثر هو هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the surah's miraculousness includes foretelling abundant followers or descendants, future capacity to sacrifice, and the enemy's eventual abasement, all fulfilled as predicted.
rows.anchor: أنا إذا حملنا الكوثر على كثرة الأتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh could not imitate even this short surah; their failure establishes the Qur'an's inimitability and thereby prophethood, monotheism, revelation, and the religion's truths.
rows.anchor: عجزوا عن معارضتها مع صغرها فبأن يعجزوا عن معارضة كل القرآن أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of the surah's three verses is independently miraculous, and the three together are miraculous too, a unique property among surahs.
rows.anchor: ثم لها خاصية ليست لغيرها وهي أنها ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is credited with interpreting al-Kawthar as all God's blessings upon Muhammad, since the word's unrestricted abundance includes every blessing.
rows.anchor: وهو المنقول عن ابن عباس لأن لفظ الكوثر يتناول الكثرة الكثيرة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: When someone reduced Ibn Abbas's view to a river in Paradise, Sa'id b. Jubayr answered that the river is one part of the abundant good given to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فقال سعيد : النهر الذي في الجنة من الخير الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers gifts already bestowed in Mecca—prophethood, Qur'an, renown, and victory—because a promised afterlife reward is not literally given yet; a parent's grant to a child shows how a promised gift can still be called given.
rows.anchor: الأقرب حمله على ما آتاه الله تعالى من النبوة والقرآن والذكر الحكيم والنصرة على الأعداء

none: Section heading introducing the commentary on 108:2; no substantive point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary reading of “pray” is perform prayer. Prayer is better than a bare command to thank because it combines inward recognition, verbal praise, and bodily service and humility.
rows.anchor: أن الشكر عبارة عن التعظيم وله ثلاثة أركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A command merely to thank might imply Muhammad had not already been grateful, whereas he knew and obeyed his Lord from the beginning; prayer itself was taught by revelation.
rows.anchor: لو قال فاشكر لكان ذلك يوهم أنه ما كان شاكرا لكنه كان من أول أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi recounts a report that Muhammad asked how to pray without ablution; Gabriel struck the ground, water sprang forth, and he was told to pray.
rows.anchor: قال محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام : كيف أصلي ولست على الوضوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Kawthar means prophethood, prayer is the noblest obedience for the Prophet to enjoin upon himself and all people.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا حملنا الكوثر على الرسالة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima interpret “pray” as “give thanks”; the immediate fa signals that gratitude must follow a blessing promptly.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : فصل لربك أي فاشكر لربك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: On this interpretation, the fa also recalls that humans were created to worship and that Muhammad was commanded to worship until death and to resume effort after finishing one task.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من فاء التعقيب ههنا الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is supplication, since prayer can mean invoking God; the fa suggests God granted abundance before Muhammad even asked.
rows.anchor: فصل أي فادع الله لأن الصلاة هي الدعاء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In support of the supplication reading, the Prophet is quoted: “Ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted”; he was always concerned for his community.
rows.anchor: سل تعطه واشفع تشفع ) وذلك لأنه كان أبدا في هم أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the ordinary legal sense of prayer because it is the most established meaning in religious usage.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القول الأول أولى لأنه أقرب إلى عرف الشرع

rows.speaker: عامة المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes understand “sacrifice” as slaughtering camels.
rows.anchor: الأول : وهو قول عامة المفسرين : أن المراد هو نحر البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second broad view takes “sacrifice” as an action connected with prayer, before, during, or after it, and reports several interpretations.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد بقوله : { وانحر } فعل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra interprets the command as facing the qibla.
rows.anchor: أحدها : قال الفراء : معناها استقبل القبلة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali says Gabriel explained that the command is to raise the hands at the opening takbir, bowing, rising, and prostrating; this adorns prayer as raising hands adorns the angels' prayer.
rows.anchor: روى الأصبغ بن نباتة عن علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Another report from Ali interprets sacrifice as placing the hands on the chest: raising them signals a seeker of refuge, while placing them there signals humility.
rows.anchor: روى عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه فسر هذا النحر بوضع اليدين على النحر في الصلاة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets the command as sitting between the two prostrations until the chest appears upright.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : قال عطاء : معناه اقعد بين السجدتين حتى يبدو نحرك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Sulayman al-Taymi interpret it as raising the hands toward the chest after supplication.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك ، وسليمان التيمي أنهما قالا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi traces these interpretations to nahr meaning the chest; “to sacrifice” here can mean to strike or reach the chest, as in expressions naming a body part that was struck.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : وأصل هذه الأقوال كلها من النحر الذي هو الصدر

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi explains the qibla interpretation as standing upright opposite the mihrab with the chest aligned to it and no turning aside.
rows.anchor: انتصاب الرجل في الصلاة بإزاء المحراب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra supports “facing” with the Arabic usage that houses or positions face one another, citing a line about the people of al-Abtah facing each other.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : منازلهم تتناحر أن تتقابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rhetorical explanation of facing the qibla says God's House and the worshipper's prayer-heart should face the qibla of divine mercy and care.
rows.anchor: الكعبة بيتي وهي قبلة صلاتك وقلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers slaughtering camels: Scripture pairs prayer with almsgiving; pagans prayed and sacrificed to idols; details of prayer already fall under “pray”; prayer glorifies God while slaughter benefits creatures; and nahr most commonly means camel sacrifice.
rows.anchor: الأكثرون حمله على نحر البدن أولى لوجوه

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: The Hanafis infer obligatory sacrifice: God commanded it, the Prophet must have obeyed, and believers must follow him according to the cited commands.
rows.anchor: استدلت الحنفية على وجوب الأضحية بأن الله تعالى أمره بالنحر

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school answers that following the Prophet is qualified by a report listing the forenoon prayer, sacrifice, and witr as duties imposed on him but not his community.
rows.anchor: وأصحابنا قالوا : الأمر بالمتابعة مخصوص بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes “pray” as prayer in general, contrasting pagans' prayer and sacrifice to idols; the verse is cited in the debate over whether a general command may be clarified later.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه أراد بالصلاة جنس الصلاة لأنهم كانوا يصلون

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the command means the five obligatory prayers, whose manner was already known, so no further explanation was needed.
rows.anchor: أجاب أبو مسلم ، وقال : أراد به الصلاة المفروضة أعني الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it as the Eid prayer with its sacrifice, since some people used to sacrifice before praying; the investigators call this weak because conjunction with waw does not establish sequence.
rows.anchor: أراد صلاة العيد والأضحية لأنهم كانوا يقدمون الأضحية على الصلاة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id b. Jubayr interprets it as praying dawn at Muzdalifa and sacrificing at Mina.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير صل الفجر بالمزدلفة وانحر بمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the general reading, since placing sacrifice beside prayer does not require that the prayer occur on the day of sacrifice.
rows.anchor: والأقرب القول الأول لأنه لا يجب إذا قرن ذكر النحر بالصلاة أن تحمل الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “for your Lord” gives prayer its life and value: outwardly beautiful prayer remains dead and rejected without orientation to God; the verse also opposes pagan worship.
rows.anchor: الفائدة الأولى : هذه اللام للصلاة كالروح للبدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām also contrasts the Prophet's sincere prayer with the hypocritical, show-seeking prayers described in the previous surah.
rows.anchor: ذكر في السورة المتقدمة أنهم كانوا يصلون للمراءآة فصل أنت لا للرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa marks both that abundant favor causes worship and that the Prophet should ignore the enemies' claim that he is cut off, remaining occupied with obedience.
rows.anchor: المسألة الخامسة : الفاء في قوله : { فصل } تفيد سببية أمرين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Because prayer follows beloved blessings, it became the Prophet's dearest activity; he prayed until his feet swelled and said he should be a grateful servant.
rows.anchor: فقال : ( أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains that the fa makes prayer a consequence of God's favors; this is the logic behind the Prophet's worship as gratitude.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فصل } اقتضت كون الصلاة من لوازم تلك النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For your Lord” instead of “for Us” is an eloquent shift from pronoun to explicit noun, adds majesty, and removes any possible ambiguity about whom the Prophet worships.
rows.anchor: إحداها : أن وروده على طريق الالتفات من أمهات أبواب الفصاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “Lord” recalls prior nurture in the gift of al-Kawthar and promises that God will continue nurturing and caring for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لأن لفظ الرب يفيد التربية المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains the pairing of prayer and sacrifice by contrasting pagan offerings, a report that the Prophet kept only what he needed and owed no zakat, and the special obligation of sacrifice upon him.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن من الناس من قال : إنه عليه السلام ما كان يدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs prized camels most; the Prophet reportedly sacrificed one hundred camels, including Abu Jahl's camel with a gold ring, until exhausted, then Ali continued, while the camels crowded the Prophet and withdrew from Ali's knife.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام أهدى مائة بدنة فيها جمل لأبي جهل في أنفه برة من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to sacrifice camels signals detachment from worldly pleasure; pairing the greatest bodily worship with the greatest sacrifice also foretells future abundance after poverty.
rows.anchor: أن أعز الأموال عند العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates prayer should precede sacrifice, not because waw itself orders events but because the Prophet said to begin with what God began with.
rows.anchor: المسألة التاسعة : دلت الآية على وجوب تقديم الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan according to the soundest opinion; its sacrifice command is a promise of political success and removal of poverty and fear.
rows.anchor: المسألة العاشرة : السورة مكية في أصح الأقوال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: A common occasion report says al-As b. Wa'il called Muhammad “abtar” after meeting him and told Quraysh he had no surviving son; Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, and most exegetes are cited for it.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي وعامة أهل التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Ka'b b. al-Ashraf came to Mecca, Quraysh boasted of their custodianship and asked if they were better than the abtar, and he agreed; 4:51 also came down.
rows.anchor: لما قدم كعب بن الأشراف مكة أتاه جمامة قريش

rows.speaker: عكرمة وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Ikrima and Shahr b. Hawshab say Quraysh called Muhammad cut off because he had departed from them, and God announced that they were the ones cut off.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث : قال عكرمة وشهر بن حوشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other occasions name Abu Jahl, who called the Prophet abtar after his son died; Abu Lahab, who said this behind his back; and Uqba b. Abi Mu'ayt as the speaker.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل فإنه لما مات ابن رسول الله قال أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says any of these unbelievers could have said it because they said worse things; al-As was likely the most persistent, explaining why reports most often identify him.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد في كل أولئك الكفرة أن يقولوا مثل ذلك فإنهم كانوا يقولون فيه ما هو أسوأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shana'an means hatred and shani' is a hater; abtar literally means cut off, especially tailless, and figuratively means without descendants or cut off from good.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : الشنآن هو البغض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic wording confines the description to the hater: the enemies meant that Muhammad had been cut off from all good or a particular good.
rows.anchor: يفيد أنه لا عالم غيره

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Quraysh used abtar for a man whose sons died; after Qasim, Abd Allah, and Ibrahim died, they claimed Muhammad had no successor, but his lineage has grown through history while theirs disappeared.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : كانت قريش يقولون لمن مات الذكور

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says abtar meant one who falls short before reaching his goal; God made the Prophet's foes defeated and humbled while Islam's banners rose.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : عنوا بكونه أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that abtar means lacking a helper: the Prophet had God, Gabriel, and righteous believers, whereas the unbelievers were left without supporters.
rows.anchor: زعموا أنه أبتر لأنه ليس له ناصر ومعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abtar can also mean contemptible and low; Razi recounts a storyteller's tale in which Abu Jahl challenged Muhammad to wrestle and was thrown down twice, linking the verse to that event.
rows.anchor: رابعها : الأبتر هو الحقير الذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the enemies' false insult will fade, while the praise bestowed on Muhammad endures forever.
rows.anchor: وأما المدح الذي ذكرناه فيك ، فإنه باق على وجه الدهر

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan b. Ali says the Umayyad kingdom appeared in a dream as men successively climbing the Prophet's pulpit; al-Kawthar and Laylat al-Qadr were revealed, and the dynasty eventually ended and became cut off.
rows.anchor: فذكر بعض القصاص أن المراد من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the enemies' insult directly, as a beloved defends a beloved; Razi compares other passages where God personally refutes accusations against prophets.
rows.anchor: الكفار لما شتموه ، فهو تعالى أجاب عنه من غير واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi adduces God's answers to charges of falsehood, madness, and rejecting messengership, including that disbelievers in the afterlife are in remote error, the Prophet is not mad, and he is truly a messenger.
rows.anchor: بل الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة في العذاب والضلال البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other divine replies reject claims that the Prophet is a mad poet, affirm truth and the messengers, deny that he was taught poetry, and call the accusation against him slander.
rows.anchor: بل جاء بالحق وصدق المرسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having given immense blessings, God also promises the Prophet's enemy will be conquered, since a blessing is incomplete while an enemy remains triumphant.
rows.anchor: لما بشره بالنعم العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One subtlety is that the enemy may live to see signs of the Prophet's success and his own affliction, dying consumed by rage.
rows.anchor: لا أفعله لكي يرى بعض أسباب دولتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the adversary a hater says his only remaining power is hatred; unable to harm the Prophet, he burns with envy, and his enmity itself brings him distress.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي يبغضك لا يقدر على شيء آخر سوى أنه يبغضك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering implies that the enemy became cut off because he hated the Prophet; hostility toward one whom God exalts is hostility toward God.
rows.anchor: ثالثها : أن هذا الترتيب يدل على أنه إنما صار أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the surah's benefits exceed what he has listed as a drop in an ocean; he then rejects Musaylima's attempted imitation.
rows.anchor: من فوائد هذه السورة كالقطرة في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaylima's parody merely borrows the surah's wording and order, so it cannot count as a true challenge or imitation.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن الألفاظ والترتيب مأخوذان من هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parody ignores how this surah completes the previous one and prepares for the next, leaving most of its subtleties unanswered.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أنا ذكرنا أن هذه السورة كالتتمة لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says a sound literary ear recognizes the vast difference between the Qur'anic declaration that the hater is abtar and Musaylima's flat claim that the enemy is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : التفاوت العظيم الذي يقر به من له ذوق سليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah answers every charge against the Prophet—no child, helper, or lasting renown—by leaving al-Kawthar unrestricted, which thus includes all worldly and afterlife good.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما لم يقيد ذلك الكوثر بشيء دون شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands encompass bodily obedience through prayer and sacrifice, wealth obedience, and inward obedience through acting solely for God; the order refutes libertines who claim inward devotion makes bodily acts unnecessary.
rows.anchor: لأن طاعة البدن هي الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām signals sincerity and refutes the libertine doctrine that inward devotion can replace the limbs' obedience; “Lord” promises care from before birth onward.
rows.anchor: فهذه اللام تدل على بطلان مذهب الإباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening shows God first pouring out blessings and the ending shows Him defending the Prophet and perfecting blessings in both worlds.
rows.anchor: هو الأول بإفاضة النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six-verse Meccan surah is also called al-Munabadhah, al-Ikhlas, and al-Muqashqishah.
rows.anchor: تسمى سورة المنابذة وسورة الإخلاص والمقشقشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says reciting it is like reciting a quarter of the Qur'an; Razi explains that Qur'anic commands and prohibitions each concern hearts and limbs, while this surah addresses prohibitions of the heart.
rows.anchor: وكل واحد منهما ينقسم إلى ما يتعلق بالقلوب وإلى ما يتعلق بالجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “Say” explains that the Prophet speaks harshly only because God ordered him, despite the Qur'an's earlier command to invite people graciously and its description of him as mercy to the worlds.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه خاطبهم بيا أيها الكافرون فكانوا يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet loved his relatives and had been told to warn his nearest kin, family ties could inhibit sternness; God therefore explicitly commanded him to speak firmly.
rows.anchor: قل لا أسئلكم عليه أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Say” emphasizes complete transmission of everything revealed, as required by the command to deliver God's message.
rows.anchor: فأمر بتبليغ كل من أنزل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Quraysh acknowledged God as creator, hearing the command “Say” showed the rebuke came from their Creator rather than Muhammad's own initiative, making it more bearable.
rows.anchor: أما لما سمعوا قوله : { قل } علموا أنه ينقل هذا التغليظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each divine command to “Say” is a fresh commission proving messengership and signaling a sovereign's special esteem for his commissioned servant.
rows.anchor: فكلما قيل له : { قل } كان ذلك كالمنشور الجديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the unbelievers proposed alternating a year of worship of each other's deities, the Prophet's answer was to convey God's direct command to reject their proposal.
rows.anchor: نعبد إلهك سنة ، وتبعد آلتنا سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God had answered their insult by declaring the Prophet's hater cut off, He now has the Prophet answer their insult to God and their attribution of partners.
rows.anchor: حين ذكروك بسوء ، فأنا كنت المجيب بنفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers falsely called the Prophet abtar, whereas he could truthfully call them unbelievers; “Say” marks the difference between the unjust insult and their actual conduct.
rows.anchor: الفرق أنهم عابوك بما ليس من فعلك وأنت تعيبهم بما هو فعلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Muhammad merely called them unbelievers, they could dispute whether this was his or God's speech; “Say” settles that God commanded him to disavow their idols.
rows.anchor: أما لما قال : قل ، سقط هذا الاعتراض لأن قوله : { قل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Say” emphasizes that the revelation must be conveyed and that the unbelievers' request was gravely objectionable.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك كالتأكيد في إيجاب تبليغ هذا الوحي إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past dissimulation under fear is no longer needed: God strengthened the Prophet with al-Kawthar and the promise that his hater is abtar, so he should speak without concern.
rows.anchor: لما قوينا قلبك بقولنا : { إنا أعطيناك الكوثر } وبقولنا : { إن شانئك هو الابتر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A direct address by God can honor and rebuke simultaneously; the fragment begins to contrast that mixed effect with the form “Say, O unbelievers.”
rows.anchor: خطاب الله تعالى مع العبد من غير واسطة يوجب التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With “Say, O unbelievers,” honor from God's address belongs to Muhammad while the humiliation of being called unbelievers belongs to the addressees, combining honor for allies and disgrace for enemies.
rows.anchor: المخاطبة إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad belonged to their tribe and was deeply compassionate and truthful; his frank description of them could persuade them to abandon the ugly trait he names.
rows.anchor: وكان في غاية الشفقة عليهم والرأفة بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rebuke from a tribesman and former neighbor is especially painful, which may drive them to examine themselves and renounce unbelief.
rows.anchor: فأنت من قبيلتهم ، ونشأت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surahs al-Asr and al-Kawthar mention faith, good works, prayer, and sacrifice; what remains is exhorting truth and patience by publicly rejecting idolatry.
rows.anchor: بقي عليك التواصي بالحق والتواصي بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the Prophet publicly denied that God had abandoned him during the pause in revelation, he should now publicly deny worshipping idols rather than leave a false impression.
rows.anchor: فلما ناديت بنفي تلك التهمة ، فناد أنت أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's silence while weighing how to answer did not imply doubt, but the unbelievers mistook it for inclination toward their faith; God commands him to remove the false impression openly.
rows.anchor: إن توقفك عن الجواب في نفس الأمر حق ولكنه أوهم باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When awe at the divine presence made the Prophet unable to praise God fully during the ascension, God tells him to give voice to repudiating His enemies; his speech and silence are both for God.
rows.anchor: لما قال له ربه ليلة المعراج : أثن علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi begins another argument: commanding the Prophet to say aloud “I do not worship what you worship” requires rejection in deed, heart, and speech, unlike merely commanding him not to worship.
rows.anchor: أما لما أمره بأن يقول بلسانه : { لا أعبد ما تعبدون } يلزمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks why Muhammad was silent and says he need not seek acceptance from the unbelievers, since He has given him al-Kawthar.
rows.anchor: قال له : يا محمد لم سكت عن الرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds Muhammad that He prioritized the Prophet over His own right; Muhammad should likewise put Gods right first and openly reject their proposal.
rows.anchor: الثاني والعشرون : أنسيت يا محمد أني قدمت حقك على حق نفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet hesitated to rebuke them for fear of alienating them, God says he need not hope in their favor or fear them: al-Kawthar is his and his enemy is cut off.
rows.anchor: أما الطمع فيما يعدونك من قبول دينك ، فلا حاجة بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God argues that hardship beside a caring parent is preferable to comfort among strangers, using the analogy to stress the Creators care over false gods.
rows.anchor: ثم العرى والجوع مع الوالد أحسن من الشبع مع الأجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols lack life and attributes, while their worshippers are empty of knowledge and piety; they cannot compete with Gods care.
rows.anchor: لأن أصنامهم جائعة عن الحياة عارية عن الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi recalls Gods nurturing of Muhammad as orphaned and needy, then His gift of faithful companions who supplied treasure, prestige, support, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: ألم أجدك يتيما وضالا وعائلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since pledging to the Prophet is pledging to God and following him is following God, the Prophet should echo God's public disavowal of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: فصرح أنت أيضا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Care from God exceeds parental care: He protected Mecca from the elephant army, provided for Quraysh journeys, gave the Prophet companions and al-Kawthar, and promised his enemy ruin, grounding exclusive worship.
rows.anchor: ألم أكف أصحاب الفيل حين حاولوا تخريب بلدتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet protested when people denied his lawful parentage; because he would reject shared lineage, he should all the more reject associating partners with God in worship.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم تسكت عند التشريك في الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator cannot be equated with a lifeless idol; Muhammad should publicly refute both idolatry and the accusation that he is mad.
rows.anchor: فحكمت بأن من سوى بين الإله الخالق وبين الوثن الجماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing the title god does not grant idols divine reality: they lack the knowledge and power required for lordship.
rows.anchor: والمشاركة في الاسم لا توجب المشاركة في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi analogizes that a woman cannot be jointly claimed by two men, nor awarded to either when both produce evidence; this illustrates why worship cannot be shared.
rows.anchor: وهو أن امرأة لو ادعاها رجلان فاصطلحا عليها لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as a slave cannot lawfully belong to two masters for intercourse, worship cannot be divided between God and an idol; agreement to alternate would itself be unbelief.
rows.anchor: والجارية بين إثنين لا تحل لواحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet offered his wives worldly life or God, himself, and the afterlife, Aisha immediately chose the latter; one should reject what opposes Gods will.
rows.anchor: فقالت : أفي هذا أستأمر أبوي بل أختار الله ورسوله والدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must avoid situations suggesting approval of idolatry; Razi also invokes the alleged satanic verse incident as a reason to remove suspicion by explicit disavowal.
rows.anchor: فإذا ثبت أنه يجب البراءة عن موقف التهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says a servants duty to the master precedes care of a child, then introduces Ali request to marry Abu Jahl daughter as an analogy for prioritizing the Lord.
rows.anchor: ثم أجمعنا على أن خدمة المولى مقدمة على تربية الولد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet refused Ali request repeatedly, explaining that Fatima was part of him and her distress was his own.
rows.anchor: لا آذن لا آذن لا آذن أن فاطمة بضعة مني

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said he would not unite the daughter of Gods enemy with the daughter of Gods beloved.
rows.anchor: والله لا يجمع بين بنت عدو الله ، وبنت حبيب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Muhammad rejected that union to protect his daughter, Razi argues he should reject shared worship even more emphatically to honor his Lord.
rows.anchor: فكأنه تعالى يقول : صرحت هناك بالرد وكررته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet reports seeing a Paradise palace for Umar but abstaining from it out of jealousy; Razi turns this into a demand to fear Gods jealousy and reject shared worship.
rows.anchor: قلت لعمر : رأيت قصرا في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Muhammad plainly refused that marriage for his daughter's sake, he should state his refusal of idol worship even more plainly for the Lord's sake.
rows.anchor: صرحت هناك بالرد وكررته على سبيل المبالغة رعاية لحق الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child instinctively resists a prettier stranger replacing the mother who nurtured him; the argument analogizes that instinct to rejecting other objects of worship.
rows.anchor: فلو أخذتك امرأة أجمل وأحسن وأكرم من أمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave life, provision, reason, guidance, and favor before any other benefactor, so He alone deserves worship.
rows.anchor: تقول لا أريد غير الأم لأنها أول المنعم علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even animals remember the one who fed them; rational humans, especially the best of creation, should not forget the greater gifts of existence, beneficence, and prophethood.
rows.anchor: قد عرفت أن الشاة والكلب لا ينسيان نعمة الإطعام ولا يميلان إلى غير من أطعهما

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i holds that inability to provide maintenance establishes a right to separation; by analogy, even if Muhammad had been attached to idols he would have had to separate, but he never was.
rows.anchor: مذهب الشافعي أنه يثبت حق الفرقة بواسطة الإعسار بالنفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Multiple deities do not add wealth or power as multiple possessions might; they are like dependents increasing need, while one God already receives all the Prophet's worship and cannot be fully thanked.
rows.anchor: ظنوا أن الكثرة في الإلهية كالكثرة في المال يزيد به الغني وليس الأمر كذلك
